title: Spanish I · Entry check
instructions: Optional orientation, not a placement certificate. If you are an absolute beginner, skip the score and begin Unit 1. Try six familiar expressions without notes, then record which skills you want to develop.
task: Record any greeting you already know. Write a learning goal and identify a realistic conversation partner or solo practice arrangement. No prior Spanish is expected.
rubric: Score task fulfillment, comprehensibility/coherence, target-language control, and responsiveness/revision separately from 0 (no evidence) to 3 (independently effective for this task). Record the evaluator: self, peer, or instructor. Solo practice cannot demonstrate live interaction.

title: Spanish I · Cumulative midterm
instructions: After Units 1–6, work without notes in assessment mode. These questions sample all six units. Then complete the writing and interaction task; report quiz accuracy separately from communication evidence.
task: Exchange names, origin, occupation, two daily habits and an appointment time with a partner. Ask five information questions and clarify one answer. Then write a 70–90-word profile of the person. Solo: invent a person and label your spoken evidence rehearsal.
rubric: Score task fulfillment, comprehensibility/coherence, target-language control, and responsiveness/revision separately from 0 (no evidence) to 3 (independently effective for this task). Record the evaluator: self, peer, or instructor. Solo practice cannot demonstrate live interaction.

title: Spanish I · Cumulative final
instructions: After Units 1–12, take one independent attempt without notes. Questions sample all twelve units; do not infer communication proficiency from the score. Save the capstone draft, revision and reflection in Unit 12 homework.
task: Write a 100–130-word personal profile covering identity, origin, location, routines, interests and a plan. Give a two-minute introduction, then answer three unprepared partner questions and negotiate an activity. Add one café request and an ingredient clarification. Keep your first and revised drafts; identify two corrections with reasons.
rubric: Score task fulfillment, comprehensibility/coherence, target-language control, and responsiveness/revision separately from 0 (no evidence) to 3 (independently effective for this task). Record the evaluator: self, peer, or instructor. Solo practice cannot demonstrate live interaction.

title: Spanish II · Entry check
instructions: Use this entry check to identify prerequisites to revisit; it is not a placement certificate.
task: Compare two work or study schedules. Ask three genuine follow-ups and agree when you can meet. Include one fact you know and one person or place you know.
rubric: Score task fulfillment, comprehensibility/coherence, target-language control, and responsiveness/revision separately from 0 (no evidence) to 3 (independently effective for this task). For source tasks also score accuracy of attribution and proportionality of conclusions from 0–3. Record self, peer or instructor evaluation. Solo rehearsal cannot demonstrate live interaction. Review the weakest dimension with a new task before reassessing.
